lines: A note-block sequencer of twelve blocks in three rows, playing one, two or three tracks out of a single polyphonic pair of jacks
One beat of the sequence, holding up to four notes in one of nine subdivisions; left click to step forward, shift and left click to step back, right click to choose from a list
Sets the pitch of one note in the block: click for a keyboard carrying Rest, Tie and an Auto Advance button, or drag up and down to set the voltage
Sets how many note blocks of each track are played before the sequence returns to the first
Steps through the track layouts: A B C gives each row a track, A A B joins rows one and two and plays row three twice a cycle, A A A makes one track of all three, Chord plays columns as chords
Advances the sequence one note block; a polyphonic cable clocks each track from its own channel
Returns the sequence to its first note block when the voltage rises past 2V; a polyphonic cable resets each track from its own channel
The pitch of the note now playing, one polyphonic channel per configured track
High while a note is playing, for the length set on the menu, one polyphonic channel per configured track
A gate at the end of each cycle, one polyphonic channel per configured track
Note — nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
Note — this build has twelve note blocks, four per row; the maker's manual says sixteen
Note — the small button above each note block is a lock, and it carries no note of its own because it is drawn inside the block rather than as a control of the module
Note — right-clicking a block, or dragging across several and right-clicking, opens a bulk edit menu for copying, pasting, randomising and shifting only those blocks
Menu — Gate Length — sets how much of each note the gate output stays high for
Menu — Swing — delays every second note block
Menu — Clock Mode: Gate, Phase — reads the clock input either as a square wave, high above 2V and low below 0.1V, or as a ramp that advances a block when it falls from above 9V to below 1V
Menu — Chord Mode — forces every row to the same subdivisions and plays each column as a chord
Menu — Randomize — randomises the pitches or the rhythm of the whole sequence
Menu — Shift & Shuffle — shifts and shuffles the sequence from the menu, the way the Shift & Shuffle expander does from its jacks
Menu — Set Rhythm — sets every note block to one subdivision
Menu — Note Pool — sets the pool of notes the randomisers draw from, from a scale, from a keyboard, or by shifting the current pool in semitones
Menu — Copy/Paste — copies and pastes the sequence or the note pool in a portable format that other JP sequencers read
Menu — Expanders — places an expander module beside this one

ThreeTrack.notes: The plugin publishes no source; everything here was read from the manual at version 2.1 revision 2 and confirmed against the installed 2.1.1 binary, which carries full C++ symbols. The clock thresholds (2.0V high, 0.1V low) are in ClockCounter::process at 0x69050 and the phase-mode rule (above 9V then below 1V) at 0x6906c-0x69080. The Lock parameter of each block and the menu-only Swing and Gate Length parameters have no census position, so they are left untagged. The manual's figure of 16 note blocks does not match this build, which configures 12 (params 0 to 119, ten per block).

WindowedSwitch.notes: Closed source; read from the maker's manual and from the installed 2.1.1 binary, which carries full C++ symbols. Inputs A and B and outputs A and B get no family: the module copies whatever is patched into them. THE PASS-THROUGH SWITCHES ARE REVERSED in this build. The gate byte at module+0x151 is what output 1, named Gate Open, is set to 10V from (0x6af8c-0x6af98). Output 3 (Output A) is written from input 2 only when that byte is zero (0x6afbc branches past the load when it is set), and output 4 (Output B) only when it is non-zero (0x6afd4). The maker's port descriptions read 'Passes Input A when Gate is Open' and 'Passes Input A when Gate is Low' (the second is also a typo for Input B), and the manual says the same. The panel groups Gate Open with the A row and Gate Low with the B row, so a person reading the panel will get it wrong too. The Mode switch prints an infinity sign for repeat and a 1 for one shot; a value of 1 is repeat, tested at 0x6ad88.

Octavator.notes: Closed source; read from the maker's manual and from the installed 2.1.1 binary, which carries full C++ symbols. The Mode parameter is parameter 13 and has no widget position in the census, so it gets no line and no tag; it is set from the menu, whose three names Absolute, Relative and Relative + Intervals are built inline at 0x4dba8, 0x4dbc4 and 0x4dbec. The panel artwork changes with the mode (res/OctavatorA.svg, OctavatorB.svg, OctavatorC.svg). Rand draws its seed from rack::system::getUnixTime (0x49e20); Reset re-runs the stored pair of seed words (0x49d84), which is what makes the pattern repeatable.
